drhp.business: Vivid Electromech Limited designs, fabricates, assembles, tests, and commissions LV and MV electrical panels and automation systems. Its products cater to power distribution, load management, process control, and industrial automation across sectors including Data Centres, Infrastructure, Solar & Renewable Energy, and Industrial Manufacturing. The company operates two integrated manufacturing facilities in Maharashtra and maintains OEM partnerships with ABB, LK, and Schneider Electric.

drhp.expansion: The company is setting up a new integrated manufacturing facility at Village Nahren, Taluka Ambernath, District Thane, Maharashtra, measuring 7,977 sq. mtrs. The facility will manufacture LV and MV electrical panels and automation systems and will be equipped with advanced fabrication and coating equipment including a PSBB line from PRIMA Power (Finland), 3D CNC busbar machines, and an automatic powder coating plant. The project aims to support manufacturing operations and improve production capacity and processes.

risks.note: Primary raw materials (CRCA sheets, GI sheets, aluminium/copper bus bars, switchgears) are subject to commodity price fluctuations. Switchgears are primarily procured from ABB India Limited with limited-duration price locking arrangements. Material costs accounted for 77.94% of total cost in FY25.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and supplier concentration

risks.note: 85.94% of domestic revenue in FY25 came from Maharashtra. Any regional economic downturn or policy change could materially impact revenue.
Data centre segment contributed 35.80% of FY25 revenue, a sharp increase from 5.38% in FY24. A slowdown in data centre capex could adversely affect growth and profitability.

The company's ability to manufacture type-tested, branded panels depends on continued OEM licences from ABB, L&T, LK, and Schneider Electric. Termination or non-renewal could impact competitive positioning.
risks.risk: Dependence on OEM partnerships for product certification and market access

risks.note: The business requires significant working capital for inventory and receivables; Rs. 4,000 lakhs of IPO proceeds are allocated to meet working capital requirements.

The proposed Ambernath facility involves a total estimated project cost of Rs. 6,673.56 lakhs. Delays in commissioning, cost overruns, or slower-than-expected ramp-up could impact returns on invested capital.
risks.risk: Execution risk on new manufacturing unit

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward-integrated, in-house manufacturing across the full production process at fully integrated units (over 34,000 sq. ft.) covering design, engineering, sheet-metal fabrication (CNC turret punching/bending), in-house copper and aluminium busbar fabrication for captive use, surface treatment and powder coating, assembly/wiring and testing. The Navi Mumbai unit performs complete fabrication and coating; prefabricated and coated components are transferred to the Pune unit for assembly. Primary raw materials (CRCA/GI sheets, aluminium/copper busbars, wires, paints) are sourced from domestic suppliers (no imports); switchgear components are procured from OEMs, primarily ABB India Limited under a limited price-locking arrangement. No forward integration into distribution is disclosed; sales are direct via an in-house sales & marketing team and the GeM portal.

overview.business_model: Provides end-to-end solutions including design, fabrication, assembly, testing and commissioning of control and automation systems and LV/MV electrical panels. LV range includes PCC, IMCC, MCC, DG Synchronization and Outdoor Panels; MV range covers 3.3 kV to 36 kV panels, VFD Panels, Control & Relay Panels, RMUs and APFC Panels. Products are type-tested under IEC standards and the Company maintains OEM associations with ABB, LK and Schneider Electric, manufacturing from two factory units in Navi Mumbai and Pune (Bhosari).

genesis.founding_story: Originally incorporated as a Private Limited Company under the name 'Vivid Electromech Private Limited' under the provisions of the Companies Act, 1956 at Bombay, Maharashtra pursuant to a certificate of incorporation dated August 10, 1990 (registration no. 11-57679) issued by the Registrar of Companies, Bombay, Maharashtra. Initial subscribers to the Memorandum of Association were Vishvanath Dayanand Attavar and Bina Vishvanath Attavar. Current Promoters are Sameer Vishvanath Attavar and Meeta Sameer Attavar. Converted to a Public Limited Company and renamed 'Vivid Electromech Limited' vide fresh certificate of incorporation dated February 12, 2025 issued by the Registrar of Companies, Central Registration Centre.

internal_operational.detail: Costs of raw materials (CRCA sheets, GI sheets, aluminium, copper bus bars, electrical wires, switchgears) are subject to volatility due to factors beyond control. No long-term contracts with suppliers; limited price locking with ABB India Limited. Inability to pass on costs may impact margins.

internal_operational.detail: Significant portion of raw materials sourced from few key suppliers, primarily in Maharashtra. No long-term purchase contracts except one renewed annually. Top 1 supplier accounted for 49.81% of purchases in Fiscal 2025. Maharashtra accounted for 52.36%, 61.48%, 62.15% of total purchases in Fiscals 2025, 2024, 2023 respectively.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on limited suppliers in concentrated geography

internal_operational.detail: Substantial portion of revenues dependent on key customers; no long-term contracts. Loss of major customers or reduction in orders could adversely impact revenues and profitability.

strategy_growth.detail: There can be no assurance that proposed new manufacturing facility will achieve projected levels of production, efficiency, or capacity utilization. Commencement may be subject to longer stabilization periods, initial operational challenges, higher-than-anticipated operating costs, or suboptimal performance of installed machinery. Commercial success depends on adequate and sustained demand; if additional capacity is not absorbed by the market, expected revenues and returns may not be generated.

strategy_growth.detail: As part of growth strategy, aim to strengthen product portfolio, focus on cost efficiencies, maintain quality standards, attract and retain skilled employees, and expand into new geographies and customer segments. Challenges include acquiring new customers, identifying requirements in different markets, obtaining approvals/certifications, estimating resources, preserving uniform culture, strengthening internal systems, recruiting/training personnel, ensuring customer satisfaction, maintaining performance/safety/quality standards. Execution requires significant capital investment and cash outlays; operating expenses and working capital requirements may increase substantially.

strategy_growth.title: Unable to manage growth effectively and further expand into new markets

strategy_growth.detail: Expansion into new export markets subjects to challenges including lack of familiarity with culture and economic conditions, language barriers, difficulties in staffing and managing operations, absence of established reputation. Risks involved may be higher than anticipated; may face significant competition. Subject to additional risks such as compliance with diverse laws, exposure to government actions, political/economic/social instability. Business is primarily domestic; minimal exports undertaken. Exposed to foreign exchange fluctuation risks to limited extent. Do not currently follow a formal hedging policy.

concerns_observed: Promoters and Promoter Group hold 99.99% pre-Offer; only seven shareholders exist, indicating extremely concentrated ownership and limited public float history.
Multiple bonus issues in capital history, including a 1:1 bonus on August 4, 2025, within 18 months of DRHP date, potentially diluting IPO subscribers' relative cost basis.
High customer concentration: Top 1 customer contributed 32.56% of revenue in FY25; Top 5 contributed 55.59%; Top 10 contributed 69.90%.
High supplier concentration: Top 1 supplier accounted for 49.81% of purchases in FY25; Top 5 accounted for 63.12%.
Geographical concentration: Maharashtra contributed 85.94% of revenue in FY25; both manufacturing units are in Maharashtra.

Significant working capital intensity: Trade receivables of Rs. 6,055.31 lakhs and inventory of Rs. 1,895.12 lakhs as of March 31, 2025, with negative cash flows from investing and financing activities in FY23-FY25.
Certain corporate records prior to 2006 are untraceable, and past non-compliances with Companies Act, 2013, and GST/TDS defaults exist.
Objects of the Offer include Rs. 4,787.95 lakhs for a new manufacturing unit, but final orders for machinery are pending, and no alternate funding source is identified.
Leased premises at Navi Mumbai (Plot A-163) are subject to an eviction suit and non-compliance with lease conditions, including unauthorized sub-licensing.
Contingent liabilities of Rs. 1,475.92 lakhs as of March 31, 2025, and outstanding direct tax demands, TDS defaults, and a GST show cause notice.

parameter_scores.basis: OEM partnerships with ABB, Schneider, L&T provide technical backing and brand association, but the business operates in a highly competitive industry with low entry barriers. No long-term contracts with customers or suppliers; dependence on a few key relationships. DRHP states 'Competitive business environment with relatively low entry barriers' and 'Dependence on OEM tie-ups' as risks.

Revenue grew 2.6x from FY23 to FY25, and PAT margin expanded sharply. However, growth was accompanied by rising customer and geographic concentration. Negative cash flows from investing and financing activities in all three reported years. Total debt of Rs. 423.11 lakhs as of Mar-25, with personal guarantees from promoters. Contingent liabilities of Rs. 1,475.92 lakhs.

Promoters hold 99.99% pre-Offer; only seven shareholders. Multiple bonus issues, including one within 18 months of DRHP. Past non-compliances with Companies Act (Sections 185, 186, 73), untraceable pre-2006 records, outstanding tax demands, TDS defaults, and GST show cause notice. KMP attrition includes four director resignations in 2022-2025. Board has 5 members with 2 independents, but committee member names not disclosed in extract.

High severity risks flagged: raw material price volatility, supplier/customer concentration, geographical concentration, working capital intensity, proposed new facility execution risk, and leased premises litigation. Active matters include an eviction suit, a civil recovery suit (Rs. 37.76 lakhs), GST show cause notice (Rs. 20.75 lakhs), and outstanding tax demands. Insurance coverage gaps noted (no machinery breakdown, no group health, no property insurance for Plot A-163).

Fresh Issue of up to 18,84,000 shares and OFS of up to 4,68,000 shares. Objects include Rs. 4,787.95 lakhs for a new unit, Rs. 975 lakhs for debt repayment, and Rs. 4,000 lakhs for working capital. No bank/institution appraisal of Objects. No alternate funding identified. Offer price not finalized; dilution percentage not determinable. Promoter average cost of acquisition is lower than face value of Rs. 10.

strengths_observed: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018 certified with ZED Bronze and SMERA SE2B rating, indicating robust quality and financial strength frameworks.

Integrated manufacturing with in-house fabrication, surface treatment, powder coating, assembly, and testing across two units in Navi Mumbai and Pune.

Zero pledging on promoter shares as per disclosed shareholding pattern.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).

sk.structure: DG sets classified by capacity: LHP (7.5-160 kVA), MHP (180-500 kVA), HHP (>500 kVA); MSLG sets 3-10 MW for continuous/base-load. Wind potential concentrated in five states: Rajasthan (24%), Gujarat (16%), Maharashtra (15%), Karnataka (15%), Andhra Pradesh (11%).
